A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Aurora and contain complete, readable main text, ten figures, five tables, and Appendices A–B. The material supports comparison across all dimensions.

before.justification: Sections 4–6 report original online adaptation and serving experiments, including acceptance-length and throughput results in Figures 3–10 and Tables 1, 4, and 5.

after.justification: The same original experiments and their reported outcomes remain in Sections 4–6 and the appendix tables.

M1.justification: The asynchronous training–serving architecture, tree attention, synchronization procedure, and acceptance/discard loss remain unchanged. The new emphasis on local traffic does not introduce a different algorithm or objective formula.

E1.justification: Both retain the same mathematics, SQL, code, finance, and conversational data, ordered and mixed traffic scenarios, and frontier-model evaluations. No dataset, domain, or evaluated task scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same no-speculation and static-speculator comparisons, scratch/pretrained Aurora configurations, and FKL, RKL, NTP, and discard variants. Comparator membership in the figures and tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: Traffic construction, model configurations, synchronization intervals, batch sizes, lookahead settings, and warm-up exclusions remain unchanged. Both use the same per-request throughput metric and Appendix B experimental settings.

E4.justification: The synchronization sweep in Figure 5, objective/discard and top-k studies in Figures 6–7, and batch-size/lookahead analyses in Figure 8 and Tables 4–5 are retained without additional tests or revised findings.

E5.justification: Both retain the same moving-average plots and throughput summaries, including P50, P05, and P95 values. No repeated-run information, seed reporting, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: The plotted results and table entries are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains batch-size-1 speedups of 1.57× for MiniMax and 1.51× for Qwen3-Coder-Next; Table 5 retains Qwen's 0.94× result at batch size 32 with lookahead 5.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(7), the acceptance approximation, loss formulation, and appendix mathematical definitions are unchanged. The new local-optimality discussion supplies conceptual motivation without new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract removes the explicit claim that rejected-token feedback improves sample efficiency. Section 1.1 more explicitly frames the contribution around rapid adaptation to local traffic. The central system, day-0 deployment, speedup claims, and conclusion remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 1.1 adds the argument that a globally optimal drafter may be inefficient for a particular serving workload, clarifying the rationale for local adaptation. Existing interpretations of synchronization costs, discard-token benefits, and batch-size limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The RPC/TensorPipe implementation, GPU allocation, optimization settings, hyperparameters, and experiment resource links remain unchanged. Appendices A–B contain the same technical and reproducibility information, apart from citation renumbering.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.3-Codex, Google AI Hypercomputer updates, and LLM Stats, while removing the Dettmers GPU guide. It adds a global-distillation versus local-traffic framing; the detailed OSD and asynchronous-RL comparisons remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The introductory argument is substantially rewritten and reorganized into algorithm-gap, system-gap, and Aurora subsections, with an extended global-versus-local traffic explanation and rewritten deployment challenges. Contribution ordering and the author list also change. Later sections largely retain their wording.

P2.justification: Existing displays move relative to the text: Figures 3–4 occupy separate pages in v2, Figures 9–10 share a page, and Table 1 precedes the batch-size discussion. Figure 2's text wrapping changes. Plot content, legends, axes, and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Sections 1.1–1.3 clarify the distinction between workload mismatch and serving constraints. Removing the abstract's general sample-efficiency assertion also moderates its emphasis on rejection feedback, consistent with Section 5's mostly marginal discard-token benefits under domain shift. These improve exposition and claim precision, while the experimental evidence and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
